reason: The cold case needs a structure, so combining the metal stock with the refrigeration insert seems like a useful start.
expectation: I expect to make a case or frame incorporating the insert, though it may still need insulation and cold packs.

alternatives.reason: Freezing the cold packs also seems necessary, but I want to build the case first.

effect: The case now has a core cradle and a rover-powered refrigeration insert that can reject heat outdoors. It still appears to need insulation and prepared cold packs.
reaction: The explanation of how the radiator works in thin air was interesting.
reason: Adding felt seems like a natural next step to reduce heat entering the cold case.
expectation: I expect the felt to insulate the case, though it may still need the cold packs.

alternatives.reason: The cold packs likely need preparation too, but I want to finish insulating the case first.

effect: The cold compartment is insulated while the radiator and power connection remain exposed, so the case can still reject heat.
reaction: Keeping the radiator exposed makes the insulation choice feel practical.
reason: Freezing the cold packs is the only available combination and seems necessary to prepare the case.
expectation: I expect the freezer to chill the packs for use in the field case.

effect: The packs are ready to absorb heat during transfers, but their capacity is limited and must be restored by refrigeration.
reaction: The distinction between temporary heat absorption and active cooling is useful.
reason: This is the only available combination, and fitting the packs into the insulated case seems necessary to prepare it for the core.
expectation: I expect a prepared cold case with the conditioned packs installed, though it may still need another step.

effect: The case is complete: active refrigeration maintains its temperature, while the packs provide a short buffer during power changes.
reaction: Fitting the cartridges around the cradle was satisfying, and their specific role made the design clearer.

mostWorthwhile.text: Preparing the cold packs was most worthwhile because it explained their limited heat-absorbing capacity and why active refrigeration is still needed.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the insulation was straightforward and predictable, though its placement around the radiator made practical sense.

surprise.text: I was interested that the case's radiator can reject heat outdoors without relying on dense, cabin-like air.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the last two combinations were the only available actions at their respective steps.

continue.text: Yes. The damaged specimen and the plan to recover untouched ice make me curious about what the core might reveal.
